answer: Each epoch the system secretly assigns three random agents as canary graders, their grading logs writing to a read-only opal chain the canaries themselves cannot mutate. At close, a lotus root audit compares each canary's grade distribution against known sybil signatures. A match inside 4 epochs triggers retroactive forfeiture of every attestation the flagged set produced, costing $8K+ in burned stake per captured identity. The attacker cannot identify the canaries without bribing 60%+ of the pool at $5K+/epoch. A quill writes freely but cannot know which nib carries ink.
